And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, David divided the families of the Levites,
and appointed from them one hundred (two hundred?) and eighty-eight praisers.
And he divided them into twenty-four courses,
and set them twelve by twelve to be praising.
And David fought with the peoples round about him,
and subdued all of them.
And in the twenty-eighth year of King David, Ephesus and also Samos were built.
And in his time was Empedocles, the great philosopher,
who was one of the five pillars of wisdom {OCR?: ܚܟܡܬܐ}:
namely, he,
and Pythagoras,
Socrates,
Plato,
and Aristotle.
And he has a certain book denying the renewal of life after death that is destined for the rational soul,
and which resembles the mind of Solomon in the book of Ecclesiastes.
And he was the first to consider
that in the divine nature there is no multiplicity of names.
And even if it is said that He is wise and good and able in power,
there are not in Him distinct meanings according to these appellations,
but He is one, simple, supreme, not admitting division in meaning or in act.
After David, Solomon his son [reigned] when he was twelve years old.
He reigned forty years,
and all the years of his life were fifty-two years.
And in the fourth year of his reign he began the building of the great temple,
and completed it in seven years,
on the mountain of the Amorites,
which is Jerusalem,
on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
Sixty cubits was its length,
and twenty its breadth,
and thirty its height.
In the thirty-fourth year of his reign, he abandoned the God of Israel,
and built altars on the mountain that is before Jerusalem to Chemosh of Moab and to Milcom of the Ammonites.
And in thirteen years he completed it {his palace}:
its length was one hundred cubits,
and its breadth fifty,
and its height thirty.

and the bronze Sea,
and the {OCR?} oxen...
